plan:
## Pitch

**Dance choreographer:** Strip it to one gesture. The sheet rises, you copy, it goes. Six parts at most: sheet frame, start-time picker, link field, copy button, failure line, close. What can the user do with each one? If a part has no answer, cut it. Keep the clip state in one object. The sheet only draws it.

**Railway signaller:** Sashiko repair leaves the mend visible. The stitches are measured and repeated, and nobody hides them. So every copy attempt gets one mark on a single rule. Copied is a solid dash. Failed is an open gap with a cross. Repaired is a dash with an overstitch on top. Every mark follows the same unit of 8px dash and 8px gap. My set: sheet, start ticks, link field, copy button, repair notice, attempt ledger. And the spacing has to follow the scale. Somebody will try 12px. Don't.

**Optical technician:** Make it strange. On failure the sheet's top edge tears, and a retry stitches it closed. My set: tearing frame, copy button, stitch-closed retry, a long-URL stress field, an expiry picker, and a "mended" badge. What about a URL with 140 characters? What about "Team only · expires never" in German? I want to know which state needs Retry and which needs Cancel, and I want the answer for every one of them.

**Satellite repair apprentice:** Press it twice before you trust it. Copy, then copy again, and both times the result has to say the same true thing. After a failure the user should feel that the panel was mended. It shouldn't feel broken. Fewer moving parts. My set: sheet, copy button, retry with a manual-select fallback, a quiet repaired line, link options, close. No tearing edges.

## Clash

**Optical technician:** The tear is the point. Failure should look like damage.

**Satellite repair apprentice:** A tearing sheet moves the whole frame on every failure. That's three animations for one blocked clipboard. The feeling it leaves is alarm.

**Dance choreographer:** Agreed. And the ledger. Does a user need history for a copy button?

**Railway signaller:** Yes. Change the expiry after copying and the link on your clipboard is stale. The ledger shows that mark struck through. That is the material. Don't cut it.

**Optical technician:** Then the notice and the ledger overlap. Both say "failed".

**Dance choreographer:** Split them. The notice holds the current attempt and offers Retry or Select link. The ledger holds the past and offers nothing but reading.

**Satellite repair apprentice:** Then the second copy of the same link should say "Copied again · same link". Two presses, one honest answer.

**Railway signaller:** And the start picker uses the same dash unit as the ledger, 5 seconds per tick. One rule for every mark.

## Decision

The team builds a share sheet for a clip editor where a visitor sets a start point and access, copies the link, and sees any clipboard failure stay visible until it is repaired by retry or manual selection.

Concept: Mended Share Sheet

The choreographer set the boundary: one sample state object (`clip`, `startSec`, `access`, `expiry`, `attempts[]`) and six views that render from it. The signaller brought the sashiko reference as a rule of measured, repeated, visible marks. That rule became a single 8px dash unit shared by the start ticks and the ledger, with no decorative patterns. The optical technician supplied the state audit: every failing state names its Retry or Cancel path, and the link field is tested with a 140-character URL. The apprentice supplied the double-press check and the manual-select fallback, and argued the tearing frame out.

Rejected direction: the torn-and-stitched sheet. It moved the frame on every failure and turned a clipboard error into spectacle. Its useful core survived as the repair notice's overstitched rule.

Reference: V&A Dundee, Stitch Style: Sashiko (https://www.vam.ac.uk/dundee/whatson/events/stitch-style-sashiko). The pack is informed by sashiko repair as a visible, repeated mark. It claims no cultural authenticity and uses no sacred imagery or traditional pattern motifs. No component_source was supplied. The bottom-sheet idea bank entry informed row 1 as an idea only. No code was copied.

Why six: each row answers a separate question. Where does the panel sit (1)? Where does playback start (2)? Who can open the link, and for how long (3)? Did the copy run (4)? What happened when it failed (5)? What has been copied so far (6)? Removing any row drops one of those answers. Adding a seventh, such as share targets, would duplicate row 4.

## Build notes

1. Use one spacing scale of 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32px. The 8px dash unit in rows 2, 5 and 6 comes from the same `--space-2` variable as the gap token.
2. Put state in `state.js` with a `subscribe` function. Each artifact file mounts its own view against a local copy of the sample state, so it works alone, and `piece.html` passes one shared instance to all six.
3. Test each action twice: copy, copy, change expiry, copy, force failure, retry, force failure twice, then Select link and Ctrl+C. Check labels at 320px using the 140-character URL and the label 'Copied again · same link'.

components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 pin pair swaps labels in a reserved width. This adds pending, timeout and version-aware repeat results.
components.usefulness: This button is the core task of the sheet.
components.creativeDifference: A second press reports whether the link changed, so pressing twice is a check rather than noise.
states: pressed: 1px sink, reached on pointer or key down
repeat: 'Copied again · same link' or 'Copied · new link'
failed: label returns to 'Copy link' and row 5 shows

components.name: Copy repair notice
components.description: Failure notice that stays until repaired by retry or manual selection, then remains as a one-line repair record.
components.purpose: Report a clipboard failure and keep it visible until it is fixed.
components.use: Clipboard access is blocked in an embedded browser. The editor taps Select link, presses Ctrl+C, and reads 'Copy failed 14:02 · repaired by hand 14:03'.
components.input: Tap Retry, Select link or Dismiss. Keyboard: Tab to each, Enter or Space. After Select link, Ctrl+C or Cmd+C in the field completes the repair.
components.outcome: Failure shows 'Couldn't copy · clipboard blocked'. A repair replaces it with one line over a dashed rule, which gains an overstitched solid segment.
components.recovery: Retry disables while pending. A second failure promotes Select link to the first button. Dismiss hides the notice and logs the attempt as failed in row 6.
components.mechanism: role=alert on failure and a polite live region on repair. A copy event listener on the link field detects manual copies. The rule is two stacked SVG dash lines using the shared 8px unit.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-27 pipeline panel retry and 2026-10-28 load stages failure. Those retry jobs. This offers a manual path and keeps the repair visible.
components.usefulness: Silent clipboard failure leads to pasting an old link.
components.creativeDifference: The failure is mended in place. The repair stays as a record and is never erased.
states: failed: message with Retry, Select link and Dismiss
failed-again: '2nd attempt failed', Select link first
dismissed: hidden, attempt logged as failed

components.name: Share attempt ledger
components.description: Row of even marks, one per copy attempt, with a readable list of time, link version and result.
components.purpose: Show what has been copied this session and whether it is still current.
components.use: An editor reads '4 attempts · 3 copied · 1 repaired · 1 outdated' before pasting into chat.
components.input: Click or tap a mark to show its detail. Keyboard: Tab into the list, Left and Right or Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Enter shows detail.
components.outcome: Detail reads '14:03 · v3 · Team only, 7 days, t=42 · repaired by retry'.
components.recovery: Clear ledger empties it and shows Undo for 5 s. Earlier marks beyond 12 collapse into '+n earlier'.
components.mechanism: An append-only attempts array in shared state. Each mark uses one shape rule: solid dash for copied, gap with a cross for failed, dash with overstitch for repaired, and strike for outdated. Each mark pairs with a word. Roving tabindex listbox.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-26 log viewer event list. That list filters many event types. This one records one action's attempts against link versions.
components.usefulness: It answers whether the clipboard still matches the screen, after the notice is gone.
components.creativeDifference: Progress is counted as real attempts in one even rule. Nothing is estimated.
states: outdated: struck mark, reached by an option change after copy

demo.sharedState: One state object for harbour-walk.mp4 (3:12): startSec 42, includeStart, access, expiry, linkVersion and attempts[]. Row 1 renders the panel. Rows 2 and 3 write link fields and bump linkVersion. Row 4 reads the link and appends an attempt. Row 5 resolves failed attempts to repaired. Row 6 renders attempts and marks any copied version below the current linkVersion as outdated. A demo toggle forces clipboard rejection.
